query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Dynamic dislocation activation with associated drag is the primary driver of strain rate sensitivity in Co‐free FeNiCrMn, with the rapid generation and interaction of dislocations under dynamic loading conditions elevating the yield and flow stresses.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast, single-phase (presumably FCC) Co‐free FeNiCrMn with a homogeneous microstructure and negligible secondary phases.
generation.intervention: Conduct uniaxial compression and tension tests spanning a wide range of strain rates (from 10^(-4) s^(-1) to >1000 s^(-1)) and temperatures, with emphasis on low-temperature tests to suppress twinning. Utilize in situ TEM and high-resolution EBSD to quantify dislocation density, arrangement, and to rule out significant twinning.
generation.conditions: Experiments performed at room temperature and at lower temperatures (to reduce twinning) as well as elevated temperatures; strain rates from quasi-static to dynamic regimes; uniform sample preparation to maintain a homogeneous initial state.
generation.structural_mediator: The evolution and density of dislocation structures, characterized by TEM and EBSD, with minimal evidence of twinning in low-temperature tests.
generation.mechanism: Under dynamic loading, the rapid nucleation and limited mobility of dislocations result in significant dislocation drag, which scales with strain rate and increases the yield and flow stresses. Temperature variations alter dislocation mobility, so tests at low temperature (where twinning is minimal) will confirm that dislocation drag is the primary rate-sensitive mechanism.
generation.predicted_outcome: A systematic and measurable increase in yield strength and strain hardening with increasing strain rate, accompanied by a higher dislocation density as observed via TEM/EBSD. At low temperatures, minimal twin activity will confirm dislocation drag as the dominant effect.
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties from quasi-static tests at room temperature, where dislocation accumulation is moderate and the flow stress increases gradually with strain.
generation.boundary: This mechanism is most valid in a homogeneous, single-phase alloy without extensive twinning or phase transformation; if precipitation or phase separation becomes significant, its influence may overshadow dislocation drag.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative separation of dislocation drag from any overlapping twinning phenomena remains challenging, especially at intermediate temperatures; extensive in situ characterization is required to resolve this.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform dynamic compression tests at various strain rates and temperatures, coupled with in situ TEM and high-resolution EBSD to quantify dislocation density. Compare these results with tests conducted at low temperature to ensure minimal twinning.
measurements: Yield strength and flow stress curves across strain rates
Quantitative TEM analysis of dislocation density
EBSD mapping of dislocation structures and confirmation of minimal twin activity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If dynamic tests do not show a statistically significant increase in dislocation density that correlates with higher yield strength, or if significant twinning is observed even under conditions designed to suppress it, then the dislocation drag hypothesis would be falsified.

The as-cast equiatomic NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy has a simple FCC crystallographic structure. Serration behavior is observed in the stress- strain curves of the as-cast NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy deformed at dynamic loadings. The yield strength of the high-entropy alloy, which distributes from 490 to 800 MPa, presents a positive relationship with the strain rates. The Johnson–Cook plastic model and the Zerilli–Armstrong plastic model of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy are obtained. However, the results predicted by Zerilli–Armstrong correspond better with the experimental results. The serration behavior of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy at a high strain rate is sensitive to the strain rates. The high density of deformation bands plays an important role in the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of the as-cast NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy deformed at dynamic loadings.
